name: Coach Rowling
philosophy: Success cannot be measured by wins alone. Our job is to be the bridge from adolescence to adulthood, forging HARD student athletes on and off the field.
shortBio: Born and raised in East Cobb, Coach Rowling played football and baseball at Walton High School and went on to play baseball at the University of Georgia. Since 2018 he has built and run the strength and conditioning program at Cambridge High School, coached special teams, served as defensive coordinator since 2023, and coached baseball.
bio: Henry Rowling's story runs through high school sports. Born and raised in East Cobb, he played football and baseball at Walton High School, where he learned what hard work, dedication and a real team look like. He says plainly that he wouldn't be the man he is today without high school football, and giving today's players that same experience is why he coaches.
He went on to the University of Georgia on a baseball scholarship, and worked as a strength and conditioning intern while he was there.

In 2018 Cambridge High School brought him in to build its strength and conditioning program, and he has run it ever since: every athlete in the building comes through it. He oversaw the weight room renovation, coached special teams, and has been Cambridge's defensive coordinator since 2023, developing six first- or second-team all-region linebackers. He also coaches baseball, so he knows what it takes to run a program in season and out. He holds an Ed.S. from Valdosta State University.

His philosophy is simple: coach the player first, demand full-speed effort, and win the details. Wins matter, and he wants banners and rings as much as anyone. But the measure he cares about most is being able to look a parent in the eye and say he made their son or daughter a better person.

principles.title: Coach the Player First
principles.text: Every kid is different. Coaching is teaching, and you have to reach each player where he is.

principles.title: Effort & Hard Work
principles.text: Mistakes are OK if they come at full speed with our best effort. We can fix mistakes. It is very hard to coach effort.

principles.title: Detail Oriented
principles.text: The little things get you beat. Do the common things uncommonly well and you have an immediate advantage.

principles.title: Grow Our Own
principles.text: We develop, win and lose with our own kids. That is what builds buy-in from the school and the community.

principles.title: Player Focused
principles.text: It is about the kids, not us. If we can't put our egos aside for them, why did we get into coaching?

principles.title: Have Fun
principles.text: It's a game. The field, the weight room and the film room should add up to an experience players look back on fondly.
